1246.subject: Physics
1246.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
1246.text: A ball impinges directly on a similar ball at rest. The first ball is brought to rest by the impact. If half of the kinetic energy is lost by impact, the value of coefficient of restitution is
1246.sol:
Let $u_1$ and $v_1$ be the initial and final velocities of ball 1 and $u_2$ and $v_2$ be the similar quantities for ball 2. Here, $u_2=0$ and $v_1=0$.
$\therefore \quad$ initial KE, $K_i=\frac{1}{2} m u_1^2+\frac{1}{2} m u_2^2=\frac{1}{2} m u_1^2$
and final KE, $K_f=\frac{1}{2} m v_1^2+\frac{1}{2} m v_2^2=\frac{1}{2} m v_2^2$
Loss of $\mathrm{KE}, \Delta K=K_i-K_f=\frac{1}{2} m u_1^2-\frac{1}{2} m v_2^2$
According to question,
$\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2} m u_1^2\right)=\frac{1}{2} m u_1^2-\frac{1}{2} m v_2^2$
( $\because$ half of its $\mathrm{KE}$ is lost by impact) or $u_1^2=2 v_2^2$ or $v_2=\frac{u_1}{\sqrt{2}}$
$\therefore \quad$ Coefficient of restitution,
$e=\left|\frac{v_2-v_1}{u_1-u_2}\right|=\frac{v_2}{u_1}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

3370.subject: Chemistry
3370.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
3370.text: Which one of the following is correct order of second ionisation potential of $\mathrm{Na}, \mathrm{Ne}, \mathrm{Mg}$ and $\mathrm{Al}$ ?
3370.sol:
The electronic configuration of $\mathrm{Na}, \mathrm{Ne}, \mathrm{Mg}$ and $\mathrm{Al}$ after the removal of an electron is as
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{Na}^{+}: 1 s^2, 2 s^2, 2 p^6 \\
& \mathrm{Ne}^{+}: 1 s^2, 2 s^2, 2 p^5 \\
& \mathrm{Mg}^{+}: 1 s^2, 2 s^2, 2 p^6, 3 s^1 \\
& \mathrm{Al}^{+}: 1 s^2, 2 s^2, 2 p^6, 3 s^2
\end{aligned}$
The ionisation energy decreases as the size of the atom/ion increases. Further ionisation energy increases with increase in nuclear charge. Since, $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ gives a stable electronic configuration hence its $\mathrm{IE}_2$ is highest among the given species and therefore the correct order of their $\mathrm{IE}_2$ is
$\mathrm{Mg} < \mathrm{Al} < \mathrm{Ne} < \mathrm{Na}$

5096.text: The $FCC -$crystal contains how many atoms in each unit cell?
5096.sol:
We know that he face-centered& cubic& $\left(FCC\right)$ unit cell can be imagined as a cube with atoms~present& on each corner as well as on each face centre.&

Now,& atom at& each face centre is shared with the& other& adjacent face centre and also each corner is shared with eight other adjacent corners making it sophisticated packing lattice.

Thus, contribution of atoms in& $FCC$~lattice& will be:

$⇒ 6 \times \dfrac{1}{2} + 8 \times \dfrac{1}{8}$

Hence, the effective~number of atoms is& $4$.

8194.subject: Mathematics
8194.text: The general solution of $\left(1+e^{\frac{x}{y}}\right) d x+e^{\frac{x}{y}}\left(1-\frac{x}{y}\right) d y=0$ is
8194.sol:
Given,
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \left(1+e^{x / y}\right) d x+e^{x / y}\left(1-\frac{x}{y}\right) d y=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad\left(1+e^{x / y}\right) d x=-e^{x / y}\left(1-\frac{x}{y}\right) d y \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d x}{d y}=\frac{-e^{x / y}\left(1-\frac{x}{y}\right)}{\left(1+e^{x / y}\right)}
\end{aligned}
$$
Putting $\quad x=v y$
Differentiating w.r.t. $y$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d x}{d y} & =v \frac{d(y)}{d y}+y \frac{d v}{d y} \\
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d x}{d y} & =v+y \frac{d v}{d y}
\end{aligned}
$$
Putting value of $\frac{d x}{d y}$ and $x=v y$ in Eq. (i)
$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d y}{d x} & =\frac{e^{-x / y}\left(1-\frac{x}{y}\right)}{1+e^{x / y}} \\
v+y \frac{d v}{d y} & =\frac{-e^v(1-v)}{1+e^v} \\
\Rightarrow \quad y \frac{d v}{d y} & =-\frac{e^v+v e^v}{1+e^v}-v \\
y \frac{d v}{d y} & =\frac{-e^v+v e^v-v-v e^v}{1-e^v} \\
\Rightarrow \quad\left[\frac{d v}{d y}\right. & =\frac{-\left[v+e^v\right]}{1+e^v} \\
\Rightarrow \quad\left[\frac{1+e^v}{v+e^v}\right] d v & =-\frac{d y}{y}
\end{aligned}
$$
Integrating both sides, we get
$$
\begin{aligned}
\int \frac{1+e^v}{v+e^v} d v & =-\int \frac{d y}{y} \\
\Rightarrow \quad \int \frac{1+e^v}{v+e^v} d v & =-\log y+\log c
\end{aligned}
$$
Put
$$
\begin{aligned}
v+e^v & =t \\
\left(1+e^v\right) d v & =d t
\end{aligned}
$$
Thus, $\quad \quad \quad \frac{d t}{t}=-\log y+\log c$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \log t=-\log y+\log c \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \log \left(v+e^v\right)=-\log y+\log c \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \log y\left(v+e^v\right)=\log c \\
&

on Comparing, we obtain

14301.text: A copper rod is moved in a magnetic field. The charge developed across its ends will be proportional to
options: rate of change of magnetic flux
14301.sol:
When a copper rod is moved in magnetic field, an emf is induced in such a way that current induced will try to oppose the motion of the rod.
As we know,

$\begin{array}{lll}$& e \propto $\frac{d \phi}{d t}$& \\
\Rightarrow & i R \propto $\frac{d \phi}{d t}$& (\because e=i R) \\
\Rightarrow & $\frac{d Q}{d t} \times$R \propto $\frac{d \phi}{d t}$& $\left(\because$i=$\frac{d Q}{d t}\right)$\\
\Rightarrow & $\frac{d Q}{d t} \propto \frac{d \phi}{d t}$&
\end{array}

Hence, charge developed across the ends of the rod will be proportional to rate of change of magnetic flux.

What is the temperature at which piston will fit into the cylinder exactly? $\left({α}_{p} = 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 5} / C ∘\right and \left{α}_{c} = 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 5} / C ∘\right)$
16536.sol:
For the piston to get fit exactly into the cylinder, the thermal expansion of the piston should be $0. 08mm$from both sides along the diameter of piston, therefore, total clearance should be $\delta = 2 \times 0. 08mm = 0. 16mm$

Now, using the formula for linear expansion due to temperature $\delta = \alpha ∆ TL$ Here, $L$ is the length of internal diameter of the cylinder, $L = 15cm = 150mm$

$⇒ 0. 16mm = \left({\alpha}_{p} - {\alpha}_{c}\right) ∆ T\left(150mm\right) ⇒ ∆ T = \dfrac{0. 16}{150 \times \left(1. 6 - 1. 2\right) \times {10}^{- 5}} = 268 ° C ⇒ {T}_{C} - {T}_{p} = 268 ° C ⋯ ⋯ \left({T}_{p} = 30 ° C\right) ⇒ {T}_{C} = {T}_{p} + 268 ° C = 298 ° C$

19873.subject: Chemistry
19873.text: During a chemical reaction $\mathrm{X} \rightarrow \mathrm{Y}$, the rates of reaction starting with initial concentrations of X as $4.0 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{M}$ and $2.0 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{M}$ are $4.8 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{ mol} \mathrm{ L}^{-1} / \mathrm{s}$ and $1.2 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{ mol} \mathrm{ L}^{-1} / \mathrm{s}$ respectively. What is the order of reaction with respect to X ?
19873.sol:
The rate law for the reaction $\mathrm{X} \rightarrow \mathrm{Y}$ is given by $r = k[X]^{n}$, where $n$ is the order of the reaction.

For the first condition:
$4.8 \times 10^{-4} = k(4.0 \times 10^{-3})^{n}$ (Equation 1)

For the second condition:
$1.2 \times 10^{-4} = k(2.0 \times 10^{-3})^{n}$ (Equation 2)

Dividing Equation 1 by Equation 2:
$\dfrac{4.8 \times 10^{-4}}{1.2 \times 10^{-4}} = \dfrac{k(4.0 \times 10^{-3})^{n}}{k(2.0 \times 10^{-3})^{n}}$

$4 = \left( \dfrac{4.0 \times 10^{-3}}{2.0 \times 10^{-3}} \right)^{n}$

$4 = (2)^{n}$

Since $4 = 2^{2}$, we have $n = 2$.

Answer: $2$

options: The reaction of $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CHCl}-\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5$ with alc. KOH on heating yields two products.
When (-)-2-bromooctane is reacted with aqueous KOH , the substitution follows $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}} 2$ mechanism and product formed is $(-)$-Octan-2-ol.
Benzylic halides show higher reactivity towards $S_N 1$ reaction.
Optically active (-)-2-Methylbu\tan^{-1}-ol on reaction with HCl yields a product $(+)$-1-Chloro-2-methylbutane.
20327.sol:
(1) Correct: Dehydrohalogenation of $C_6H_5CH_2-CHCl-C_6H_5$ with alc. KOH gives stilbene (C_6H_5-CH=CH-C_6H_5$), which exists as two geometric isomers (cis and trans) — hence two products.

(2) Incorrect: $S_N2$ involves Walden inversion. Reaction of $(-)$-2-bromooctane with aqueous KOH via $S_N2$ gives $(+)$-octan-2-ol (inverted configuration), not $(-)$-octan-2-ol.

(3) Correct: Benzylic halides readily undergo $S_N1$ because the benzylic carbocation intermediate is stabilised by resonance with the benzene ring.

(4) Correct: Reaction of $(-)$-2-methylbu\tan^{-1}-ol with HCl replaces $-OH$ at the primary carbon $C_1$. No bond at the chiral centre $C_2$ is broken, so configuration is retained. However the sign of optical rotation changes, giving $(+)$-1-chloro-2-methylbutane.

The incorrect statement is (2).$

20769.text: The Bohr orbit of the hydrogen atom (n=1) is 0.530 Å. The radius of the first excited state orbit in Å is:
20769.sol:
The radius of the $n$ th Bohr orbit for a hydrogen-like species is given by $r_n = r_1 \times \dfrac{n^2}{Z}$.

For a hydrogen atom, $Z = 1$.

The first excited state corresponds to $n = 2$.

Given $r_1 = 0.530$ Å.

Substituting the values, we get $r_2 = 0.530 \times \dfrac{2^2}{1} = 0.530 \times 4 = 2.12$ Å.

Answer: $2.12$

The matrix $A$ is a scalar matrix of order $n=3$, given by $A = aI$, where $I$ is the identity matrix of order $3$.

The determinant of $A$ is $|A| = \begin{vmatrix} a \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 0 \\ 0 \text{ and } a \text{ and } 0 \\ 0 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } a \end{vmatrix} = a^3$.

Substituting $n=3$ and $|A| = a^3$ into the formula:

Answer: $a^6$

21781.subject: Mathematics
21781.sol:
Given $Q = P^T A P$.

We need to evaluate $P Q^{2014} P^T$.

Note that $Q^2 = (P^T A P)(P^T A P) = P^T A (P P^T) A P$.

Since $P$ is an orthogonal matrix, $P P^T = I$, where $I$ is the identity matrix.

Thus, $Q^2 = P^T A^2 P$.

By induction, $Q^n = P^T A^n P$ for any positive integer $n$.

Therefore, $Q^{2014} = P^T A^{2014} P$.

Substituting this into the expression $P Q^{2014} P^T$, we get $P (P^T A^{2014} P) P^T$.

Using the associative property of matrix multiplication, $(P P^T) A^{2014} (P P^T) = I A^{2014} I = A^{2014}$.

For the matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$, we observe $A^n = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2n \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$.

Thus, $A^{2014} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \times 2014 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 4028 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$.

Answer: $\left(\begin{array}{cc} 1 & 4028 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right)$

22051.subject: Mathematics
22051.text: $\text{ If } a \mathcal{N}=\{a x: x \in \mathcal{N}\} \text{, then } 3 \mathcal{N} \cap 7 \mathcal{N} \text{$ is }
22051.sol:
The set $a\mathcal{N}$ is defined as the set of all multiples of $a$ where $a \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\mathcal{N} = \{1, 2, 3, \dots\}$.

The set $3\mathcal{N}$ consists of all natural numbers that are multiples of $3$, i.e., $3\mathcal{N} = \{3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, \dots\}$.

The set $7\mathcal{N}$ consists of all natural numbers that are multiples of $7$, i.e., $7\mathcal{N} = \{7, 14, 21, 28, 35, \dots\}$.

The intersection $3\mathcal{N} \cap 7\mathcal{N}$ consists of all natural numbers that are multiples of both $3$ and $7$.

A number is a multiple of both $3$ and $7$ if and only if it is a multiple of the least common multiple of $3$ and $7$. Since $3$ and $7$ are coprime, $\text\lcm(3,7) = 3 \times 7 = 21$.

Therefore, $3\mathcal{N} \cap 7\mathcal{N} = 21\mathcal{N}$.

Answer: $21 \mathcal{N}$

22435.subject: Physics
22435.text: The shortest wavelengths of Paschen, Lymen and Balmer series are in the ratio
22435.sol:
The wavelength $\lambda$ for a transition in a hydrogen-like atom is given by the Rydberg formula: $\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R Z^2 \left( \dfrac{1}{n_1^2} - \dfrac{1}{n_2^2} \right).

For the shortest wavelength of any series, the transition occurs from $n_2 = $\infty$ to n_1$. Thus, \dfrac{1}{\lambda_{min}} =$R $\left( \dfrac{1}{n_1^2} \right)$, which implies $\lambda_{min} = \dfrac{n_1^2}{R}$.

For the Paschen series, $n_1 = 3$, so $\lambda_{Paschen} = \dfrac{3^2}{R} = \dfrac{9}{R}$.

For the Lyman series, $n_1 = 1$, so $\lambda_{Lyman} = \dfrac{1^2}{R} = \dfrac{1}{R}$.

For the Balmer series, $n_1 = 2$, so $\lambda_{Balmer} = \dfrac{2^2}{R} = \dfrac{4}{R}$.

The ratio of the shortest wavelengths of Paschen, Lyman, and Balmer series is $\lambda_{Paschen} : \lambda_{Lyman} : \lambda_{Balmer} = \dfrac{9}{R} : \dfrac{1}{R} : \dfrac{4}{R} = 9 : 1 : 4$.

Answer: $9: 1: 4$

23134.subject: Physics
23134.text: In to a vessel containing pure water a clean glass tube of radius $3.6 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{ m}$ is held vertically with 12 cm of the tube above the water level. Now the capillary tube is moved down in to the water so that only 2 cm of its length is above the water surface. Angle of contact $\theta$ at this position is (given surface tension of water $=7.2 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{Nm}^{-1}$ and $g=10 \mathrm{ ms}^{-2}$)
23134.sol:
The capillary rise $h$ in a tube of radius $r$ is given by the formula $h = \dfrac{2T \cos \theta}{r \rho g}$, where $T$ is the surface tension, $\theta$ is the angle of contact, $\rho$ is the density of water, and $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity.

First, calculate the maximum capillary rise $h_\max$ for pure water in a glass tube, where $\theta = 0^{{}^{\circ}}$ and $\cos 0^{{}^{\circ}} = 1$. Given $T = 7.2 \times 10^{-2} \text{ N/m}$, $r = 3.6 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$, $\rho = 1000 \text{ kg/m}^3$, and $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$:

$h_\max = \dfrac{2 \times 7.2 \times 10^{-2}}{3.6 \times 10^{-4} \times 1000 \times 10} = \dfrac{14.4 \times 10^{-2}}{3.6 \times 10^0} = 4 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m} = 4 \text{ cm}$.

When the tube is pushed down such that only $2 \text{ cm}$ is above the water surface, the water cannot rise higher than the top of the tube. The water will rise to the top of the tube, and the meniscus will adjust its curvature to satisfy the equilibrium condition $h' = \dfrac{2T \cos \theta}{r \rho g}$, where $h' = 2 \text{ cm}$.

Substituting the values: $2 \times 10^{-2} = \dfrac{2 \times 7.2 \times 10^{-2} \cos \theta}{3.6 \times 10^{-4} \times 1000 \times 10}$.

$2 \times 10^{-2} = \dfrac{14.4 \times 10^{-2} \cos \theta}{3.6} = 4 \times 10^{-2} \cos \theta$.

Therefore, $\cos \theta = \dfrac{2 \times 10^{-2}}{4 \times 10^{-2}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

This gives $\theta = 60^{{}^{\circ}}$.

Answer: $\theta=60^{{}^{\circ}}$

23992.subject: Chemistry
23992.text: The rate constant of a reaction at 600 K with an activation energy of $191.47$ kJ mol^{-1}$ is 5.0 \times 10^{-5}$ s^{-1}$. What is the temperature at which the half-life of the reaction becomes 152 s? [Consider pre-exponential factor and activation energy to be independent of temperature. $R = 8.314$ J K^{-1}$ mol^{-1}$]$
23992.sol:
From the unit of the rate constant (s$^{-1}$), the reaction is of first order.

The rate constant at temperature $T_2$ is:

$k_2 = \dfrac{0.693}{t_{1/2}} = \dfrac{0.693}{152} \approx 4.56 \times 10^{-3}$ s$^{-1}$

Using the Arrhenius equation:

$\log \left( \dfrac{k_2}{k_1} \right) = \dfrac{E_a}{2.303 R} \left( \dfrac{1}{T_1} - \dfrac{1}{T_2} \right)$

Substituting the given values:

$\dfrac{E_a}{2.303 R} = \dfrac{191.47 \times 10^3}{2.303 \times 8.314} = \dfrac{191470}{19.147} = 10000$ K

$\log \left( \dfrac{4.56 \times 10^{-3}}{5.0 \times 10^{-5}} \right) = 10000 \left( \dfrac{1}{600} - \dfrac{1}{T_2} \right)$

$\log (91.2) = 10000 \left( \dfrac{1}{600} - \dfrac{1}{T_2} \right)$

$1.96 = 10000 \left( \dfrac{1}{600} - \dfrac{1}{T_2} \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{600} - \dfrac{1}{T_2} = 0.000196$

$\dfrac{1}{T_2} = \dfrac{1}{600} - 0.000196 = 0.001667 - 0.000196 = 0.001471$ K$^{-1}$

$T_2 = \dfrac{1}{0.001471} \approx 680$ K

Answer: $680$ K

26009.text: Consider an $LC$ circuit, with inductance $L = 0 . 1H$ and capacitance $C = {10}^{- 3}F$, kept on a plane. The area of the circuit is $1{m}^{2}$. It is placed in a constant magnetic field of strength ${B}_{0}$ which is perpendicular to the plane of the circuit. At time $t = 0$, the magnetic field strength starts increasing linearly as $B = {B}_{0} + \betat$ with $\beta = 0 . 04T{s}^{- 1}$. The maximum magnitude of the current in the circuit is____$mA$.
26009.sol:
Emf induced in the circuit is

$\left|E\right| = \left|\dfrac{dϕ}{dt}\right| = \dfrac{d}{dt}\left[\left({B}_{0} + \betat\right)A\right]$

$= \beta \times A$

$= 0 . 04V$

So the circuit can be rearranged as

Using Kirchhoff's law we can write

$E = L\dfrac{di}{dt} + \dfrac{q}{C}$

$L\dfrac{di}{dt} = E - \dfrac{q}{C}$

For maximum current, $\dfrac{d i}{d t} = 0$,

Or $q = CE$

Using work energy theorem,

$qE = \dfrac{1}{2}L{i}^{2} + \dfrac{{q}^{2}}{2C}$

At ${i}_{max}$, $CEE = \dfrac{1}{2}L{i}_{max}^{2} + \dfrac{{E}^{2}{C}^{2}}{2C}$

Or, ${i}_{max} = \sqrt{\dfrac{C}{L}}E$

So, ${i}_{max} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{10}^{- 3} \times 0 . 04}{0 . 1 \times {10}^{- 3}}}$$= 4mA$

26258.subject: Physics
26258.text: Two satellites $P$ and $Q$ are moving in different circular orbits around the Earth(radius $R$). The heights of $P$ and $Q$ from the Earth surface are ${h}_{P}$ and ${h}_{Q}$, respectively, where ${h}_{P} = \dfrac{R}{3}$. The accelerations of $P$ and $Q$ due to Earth’s gravity are ${g}_{P}$ and ${g}_{Q}$, respectively. If $\dfrac{{g}_{P}}{{g}_{Q}} = \dfrac{36}{25}$, what is the value of ${h}_{Q}$?
26258.sol:
Acceleration due to gravity at any height from the Earth's surface is given by, $g = \dfrac{GM}{{r}^{2}}$, where $r =$distance from the centre of the Earth.

Now, we can write

$\dfrac{{g}_{P}}{{g}_{Q}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{GM}{{\left({r}_{P}\right)}^{2}}}{\dfrac{GM}{{\left({r}_{Q}\right)}^{2}}} ⇒ \dfrac{36}{25} = {\left(\dfrac{{r}_{Q}}{{r}_{P}}\right)}^{2} ⇒ \dfrac{{r}_{Q}}{{r}_{P}} = \dfrac{6}{5} ⇒ {r}_{Q} = \dfrac{6}{5} \times \left(R + \dfrac{R}{3}\right) ⇒ R + {h}_{Q} = \dfrac{8}{5}R ⇒ {h}_{Q} = \dfrac{3}{5}R$

26480.subject: Physics
26480.text: A tank contains two immiscible liquids of densities $6\rho$ and $2\rho$. The higher density liquid is filled up to a height $L/2$ from the bottom. A thin rod of density $\rho$ and length $L$ is fully immersed and hinged at the bottom so that it can oscillate freely, as shown in the figure. If the rod is slightly disturbed from its equilibrium, the time period of small oscillations is $\dfrac{2\pi}{n}\sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}}$, where $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity. The value of $n$ is:
26480.sol:
Let $A$ be the cross-sectional area of the rod.

Mass of the rod, $M = \rho A L$.

Weight of the rod, $W = \rho A L g$, acting at a distance $L/2$ from the hinge.

When the rod is displaced by a small angle $\theta$, the restoring torque is provided by the buoyant forces from the two liquids.

Buoyant force due to the lower liquid, $F_{B1} = (6\rho) A (L/2) g = 3\rho A L g$.

This force acts at the center of the immersed part in the lower liquid, which is at a distance $L/4$ from the hinge.

Torque due to $F_{B1}$ is $\tau_{B1} = F_{B1} (L/4) \theta = (3\rho A L g) (L/4) \theta = \dfrac{3}{4} \rho A L^2 g \theta$.

Buoyant force due to the upper liquid, $F_{B2} = (2\rho) A (L/2) g = \rho A L g$.

This force acts at the center of the immersed part in the upper liquid, which is at a distance $L/2 + L/4 = 3L/4$ from the hinge.

Torque due to $F_{B2}$ is $\tau_{B2} = F_{B2} (3L/4) \theta = (\rho A L g) (3L/4) \theta = \dfrac{3}{4} \rho A L^2 g \theta$.

Destabilizing torque due to gravity is $\tau_g = W (L/2) \theta = (\rho A L g) (L/2) \theta = \dfrac{1}{2} \rho A L^2 g \theta$.

Net restoring torque, $\tau_{net} = \tau_{B1} + \tau_{B2} - \tau_g = \left(\dfrac{3}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) \rho A L^2 g \theta = \rho A L^2 g \theta$.

Moment of inertia of the rod about the hinge, $I = \dfrac{M L^2}{3} = \dfrac{\rho A L^3}{3}$.

The equation of motion is $I \alpha = -\tau_{net}$

$\dfrac{\rho A L^3}{3} \alpha = -\rho A L^2 g \theta$

$\alpha = -\dfrac{3g}{L} \theta$

This represents simple harmonic motion with $\omega^2 = \dfrac{3g}{L}$.

Time period, $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = \dfrac{2\pi}{\sqrt{3}} \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}}$.

Answer: $\sqrt{3} = 1.73$

27403.text: Which of the following amino acid will give violet coloured complex with neutral ferric chloride solution?
27403.sol:
Neutral ferric chloride ($\text{FeCl}_3$) solution gives a characteristic violet coloured complex with compounds containing a phenolic hydroxyl group.

Among the given amino acids, Tyrosine contains a phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group in its side chain.

Threonine and Serine contain aliphatic $-\text{OH}$ groups, and Cysteine contains a thiol ($-\text{SH}$) group, none of which give a positive neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$ test.

Therefore, Tyrosine will give a violet coloured complex with neutral ferric chloride solution.

Answer: Tyrosine

27404.subject: Chemistry
27404.text: Consider the following reactions. Total number of electrons in the $\pi$ bonds and lone pair of electrons in the product $(X)$ is :
27404.sol:
Step 1: The starting material is an aldohexose (like D-glucose). On prolonged heating with $HI$, it undergoes reduction to form n-hexane. This indicates that all six carbon atoms are linked in a straight chain.
$\text{CHO}-(\text{CHOH})_4-\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{HI, } \Delta} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$ (n-hexane)

Step 2: n-Hexane, when passed over heated $V_2O_5$ at $773 \text{ K}$ and $10-20 \text{ atm}$ pressure, undergoes aromatization (dehydrogenation and cyclization) to form benzene.
$\text{n-hexane} \xrightarrow{V_2O_5, \text{ 773 K, 10-20 atm}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_6$ (Benzene)

Step 3: Benzene reacts with benzoyl chloride ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCl}$) in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form benzophenone. This is a Friedel-Crafts acylation reaction.
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCl} \xrightarrow{\text{Anhyd. AlCl}_3} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{CO}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$ (Benzophenone)

Step 4: Analyze the product (X), which is benzophenone.
The structure of benzophenone consists of two phenyl rings attached to a carbonyl group.
- Each phenyl ring contains $3$ $\pi$ bonds, so two rings have $6$ $\pi$ bonds.
- The carbonyl group ($\text{C=O}$) contains $1$ $\pi$ bond.
- Total number of $\pi$ bonds = $6 + 1 = 7$.
- Total number of $\pi$ electrons = $7 \times 2 = 14$.
- The oxygen atom in the carbonyl group has $2$ lone pairs of electrons.
- Total number of lone pair electrons = $2 \times 2 = 4$.

Total number of electrons in the $\pi$ bonds and lone pairs = $14 + 4 = 18$.

Answer: $18$

28365.text:
Match List I with List II :

List I List II
A. Saccharin I. High potency sweetener
B. Aspartame II. First artificial sweetening agent
C Alitame III. Stable at cooking temperature
D. Sucralose IV. Unstable at cooking temperature

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
28365.sol:
Saccharin is an artificial sweetener that is commonly used as a sugar substitute. It is about $300 - 400$ times sweeter than sugar and has a slightly bitter aftertaste.

Aspartame use is limited to cold foods and soft drinks because it is unstable at cooking temperature.

Alitame is high potency sweetener, which means that only a small amount is needed to achieve the same level of sweetness as sugar.

32882.text: Let $S$ be the set of all the natural numbers, for which the line $\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{b} = 2$ is a tangent to the curve ${\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)}^{n} + {\left(\dfrac{y}{b}\right)}^{n} = 2$ at the point $\left(a, b\right), ab \ne 0 .$ Then
32882.sol:
${\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)}^{n} + {\left(\dfrac{y}{b}\right)}^{n} = 2$

Differentiating, we get,

$n{\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)}^{n - 1} ⋅ \dfrac{1}{a} + n ⋅ {\left(\dfrac{y}{b}\right)}^{n - 1} ⋅ \dfrac{1}{b} ⋅ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{- \dfrac{1}{a}{\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)}^{n - 1}}{\dfrac{1}{b}{\left(\dfrac{y}{b}\right)}^{n - 1}} = \dfrac{- b}{a}{\left(\dfrac{xb}{ya}\right)}^{n - 1} ⇒ {\left\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right|}_{\left(a, b\right)} = \dfrac{- b}{a}{\left(\dfrac{ab}{ba}\right)}^{n - 1} = \dfrac{- b}{a}$

So, equation of the tangent to the curve at $\left(a, b\right)$ will be $y - b = \dfrac{- b}{a}\left(x - a\right) ⇒ \dfrac{y}{b} - 1 = - \dfrac{x}{a} + 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{b} = 2$

i.e. $S \in N$

33440.text: Let the coefficients of third, fourth and fifth terms in the expansion of ${\left(x + \dfrac{a}{{x}^{2}}\right)}^{n}, x \ne 0,$ be in the ratio $12: 8: 3 .$ Then the term independent of $x$ in the expansion, is equal to _______.
33440.sol:
The general term in the expansion of ${\left(a + b\right)}^{n}$ is ${T}_{r + 1} = Cr n {a}^{n - r}{b}^{r} .$

Hence, the general term in the expansion of ${\left(x + \dfrac{a}{{x}^{2}}\right)}^{n}$ is ${T}_{r + 1} = Cr n ( x{)}^{n - r}{\left(\dfrac{a}{{x}^{2}}\right)}^{r}$

$⇒ {T}_{r + 1} = Cr n {a}^{r}{x}^{n - 3r}$

Given the coefficients of third, fourth and fifth terms are in the ratio $12: 8: 3$

$⇒ \left(C2 n {a}^{2}\right): \left(C3 n {a}^{3}\right): C4 n {a}^{4} = 12: 8: 3$

$⇒ \dfrac{C2 n {a}^{2}}{C3 n {a}^{3}} = \dfrac{12}{8}$ and $\dfrac{C3 n {a}^{3}}{C4 n {a}^{4}} = \dfrac{8}{3}$

Using $\dfrac{Cr n}{Cr + 1 n} = \dfrac{r + 1}{n - r},$

$⇒ \dfrac{3}{\left(n - 2\right)a} = \dfrac{3}{2}$ and $\dfrac{4}{\left(n - 3\right)a} = \dfrac{8}{3}$

On dividing the two equations, we get $\dfrac{3\left(n - 3\right)}{4\left(n - 2\right)} = \dfrac{9}{16}$

$⇒ 4n - 12 = 3n - 6$

$⇒ n = 6$ and $a = \dfrac{1}{2} .$

For term independent of $x ⇒ n = 3r$

$⇒ r = 2 .$

$∴$ The coefficient is$C2 6 {\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{15}{4} .$

Hence, the nearest integer is $4 .$

33972.sol:
For $x > 0$: $\sin x - \frac{1}{2}\sin 2x = \sin x(1 - \cos x)$.
$\lim_{x \to 0^+} \frac{\sin x(1-\cos x)}{x^3} = \lim_{x \to 0^+} \frac{\sin x}{x} \cdot \frac{1-\cos x}{x^2} = 1 \cdot \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{2}$.
So $a = \frac{1}{2}$.
For $x < 0$ near $0$: $\frac{\pi}{2}(\cos x + \sin x)\cos x \to \frac{\pi}{2}$ from below, so $\left[\frac{\pi}{2}(\cos x + \sin x)\cos x\right] = 1$.
$f(x) = b^2 \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} \cdot 1\right) = b^2$.
For continuity: $b^2 = a = \frac{1}{2}$.
$a^2 + b^2 = \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{4}$.

36748.text: If $A$and $B$ are two events such that $P\left(A ∪ B\right) = P\left(A ∩ B\right)$, then the incorrect statement amongst the following statements is :
36748.sol:
$P\left(A ∪ B\right) = P\left(A ∩ B\right)$

Using the addition theorem of probability,

$P\left(A ∪ B\right) = P\left(A\right) + P\left(B\right) - P\left(A ∩ B\right)$

$⇒ P\left(A\right) = P\left(B\right)$

$P\left(A ∩ {B}^{'}\right) = 0$

$P\left({A}^{'} ∩ B\right) = 0$

Here, $A$ and $B$ are equally likely.

But we can't say that $P\left(A\right) = P\left(B\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Therefore, $P\left(A\right) + P\left(B\right) \ne 1$

Consider a group of three students $A, B$ and an other student in between $A$ and $B$. Choice for a student between $A$ and $B$ is 4. $A$ and $B$ can interchange their places in the group in 2 ways.
Now the group of three students (student $A$, student $B$ and a student in between $A$ and $B$ ) and the remaining 3 students can be stand in a row in 4 ! ways.
Hence total number of ways to stand in a row such that $A$ and $B$ are separated with one student in between them $=4 \times 2 \times 4$ !
Now total number of ways to stand 6 student stand in a row without any restriction $=6 !$
Hence required probability

=$\frac{4 \times 2 \times 4 !}{6 !}=\frac{4 \times 2}{6 \times 5}=\frac{4}{15}$

37421.text: The number of elements in the set ${ n \in \mathbb{N}: 10 \le n \le 100$ and ${3}^{n} - 3$ is a multiple of $7 }$ is _______.
37421.sol:
Given that $n \in \left[10, 100\right]$ and $n \in N$.

Let us take the values of $n = 1, 2, 3, . . .$ and check whether ${3}^{n} - 3$ is divisible by $7$ or not.

$⇒ {3}^{1} - 3 = 0$ is divisible by $7$

$⇒ {3}^{2} - 3 = 3$, $3$ is not divisible by $7$

$⇒ {3}^{6} = 7k + 1$ is not divisible by $7$

$⇒ {3}^{7} = 7\alpha + 3$,

$⇒ {3}^{7} - 3 = 7\alpha$ is divisible by $7$

Similarly $⇒ {3}^{13} = \left(7k + 1\right)\left(7\alpha + 3\right)$

$= 7\beta + 3$

$⇒ {3}^{13} - 3 = 7\beta$ is divisible by $7$

If we observe the pattern for $n = 1, 7, 13$, ${3}^{n} - 3$ is divisible by $7$.

That means the series forms an AP with $d = 6$.

Also $n \in \left[10, 100\right]$

The required progression is $13, 19, . . . . . . {a}_{n}$

$⇒ {a}_{n} = 13 + \left(n - 1\right)6$

But $13 + \left(n - 1\right)6 < 100$

$⇒ n < 15 . 5$

$⇒ n = 15 \in N$

Therefore, the required answer is $15$.

Now finding discriminant $D = 9 - 4 \times 2\left(- k\right)$

And $9 - 4 \times 2\left(- k\right) a perfect square$ for $any possible \left(a, b\right) as \left(a - b\right) will be a integer,

So,$9 + 8k$ is a perfect square

$⇒ k = 0 or k = 2$

Now for $k = 0$,

$2{$\left(a - b\right)$}^{2} + 3$\left(a - b\right)$ = 0$

$⇒ $\left(a - b\right)\left[2{\left(a - b\right)$}^{2} + 3\right] = 0$

$⇒ a - b = 0 ⇒ ( a, b ) \in { ( 1, 1 ) , ( 2, 2 ) \ldots . ( 10, 10 ) }$

$⇒$Total $10$ elements belonging to $R .

And, $a - b = \dfrac{3}{2}$ is not possible

Now for $k = 2$,

$2{\left(a - b\right)}^{2} + 3\left(a - b\right) - 2 = 0$

⇒ a - b = - 2 or $a - b = \dfrac{1}{2}$ (not possible)

Now for $a - b = - 2$ possible pair will be,

$⇒ ( a, b ) \in { ( 1, 3 ) , ( 2, 4 ) , \ldots . ( 8, 10 ) }$

$⇒ 8$ elements belonging to $R$

Total number of elements will be$= 18$

37582.text: Consider a set of $3n$ numbers having variance $4 .$ In this set, the mean of first $2n$ numbers is $6$ and the mean of the remaining $n$ numbers is $3 .$ A new set is constructed by adding $1$ into each of the first $2n$ numbers, and subtracting $1$ from each of the remaining $n$ numbers. If the variance of the new set is $k,$ then $9k$ is equal to ______.
37582.sol:
Let, the number be ${a}_{1}, {a}_{2}, {a}_{3}, . . . , {a}_{2n}, {b}_{1}, {b}_{2}, {b}_{3}, . . . , {b}_{n} .

Given, the mean of the first $2n$ numbers is $6$ and that of the remaining $n$ numbers is $3,$ then by using the formula for combined mean, we get, the mean of the complete set as $\mu = $\dfrac{2n \times 6 + n \times 3}{2n + n} = \dfrac{15n}{3n} =$5 .

Also, the variance is defined as ${\sigma}^{2} = \dfrac{∑ {\left({x}_{i}\right)}^{2}}{n} - {\left(\mu\right)}^{2}$

$4 = \dfrac{∑ {\left({a}_{i}\right)}^{2} + ∑ {\left({b}_{i}\right)}^{2}}{3n} - ( 5{)}^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{∑ {\left({a}_{i}\right)}^{2} + ∑ {\left({b}_{i}\right)}^{2}}{3n} = 29$

$⇒ ∑ {\left({a}_{i}\right)}^{2} + ∑ {\left({b}_{i}\right)}^{2} = 87n . . . \left(i\right)$

Now, as per the given information, the distribution becomes

${a}_{1} + 1, {a}_{2} + 1, {a}_{3} + 1, . . . , {a}_{2n} + 1, {b}_{1} - 1, {b}_{2} - 1, . . . , {b}_{n} - 1$

Thus, the new variance is

$k = \dfrac{∑ ( {a}_{i} + 1{)}^{2} + ∑ ( {b}_{i} - 1{)}^{2}}{3n} - {\left(\dfrac{\left(12n + 2n\right) + \left(3n - n\right)}{3n}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ k = \dfrac{\left(∑ {\left({a}_{i}\right)}^{2} + 2n + 2 ∑ {a}_{i}\right) + \left(∑ {\left({b}_{i}\right)}^{2} + n - 2 ∑ {b}_{i}\right)}{3n} - {\left(\dfrac{16}{3}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ k = \dfrac{∑ {\left({a}_{i}\right)}^{2} + ∑ {\left({b}_{i}\right)}^{2} + 3n + 2 ∑ {a}_{i} - 2 ∑ {b}_{i}}{3n} - {\left(\dfrac{16}{3}\right)}^{2}$

On putting the given values and value from the equation $\left(i\right),$

$⇒ k = \dfrac{87n + 3n + 2 ( 12n ) - 2 ( 3n )}{3n} - {\left(\dfrac{16}{3}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ k = \dfrac{108}{3} - {\left(\dfrac{16}{3}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ 9k = 3 ( 108 ) - ( 16{)}^{2}$

$⇒ 9k = 324 - 256 = 68 .

$

39094.subject: Physics
39094.text: A parallel plate air capacitor is connected to a battery. The plates are pulled apart at uniform speed $v$. If $x$ is the separation between the plates at any instant, then the time rate of change of electrostatic energy of the capacitor is proportional to $x^\alpha$, where $\alpha$ is _____.
39094.sol:
The electrostatic energy of a parallel plate capacitor is given by $U = \dfrac{1}{2} C V^2$.

For a parallel plate capacitor, the capacitance is $C = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{x}$, where $x$ is the separation between the plates.

Since the capacitor remains connected to the battery, the potential difference $V$ across the plates is constant.

Substituting $C$ into the energy equation gives:

$U = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A V^2}{2x}$

Differentiating $U$ with respect to time $t$ to find the time rate of change of electrostatic energy:

$\dfrac{dU}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt} \left( \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A V^2}{2x} \right) = -\dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A V^2}{2x^2} \dfrac{dx}{dt}$

Given that the plates are pulled apart at a uniform speed $v$, we have $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = v$.

$\dfrac{dU}{dt} = -\dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A V^2 v}{2x^2}$

From the above expression, it is clear that $\dfrac{dU}{dt} \propto x^{-2}$.

Comparing this with $x^\alpha$, we get $\alpha = -2$.

Answer: $-2$

41197.text:
A wedge $Y$ with mass of $10$ kg and all frictionless surfaces and the inclined surface making $37°$ with horizontal. A block $X$ with mass $2$ kg is placed at the highest point of the wedge as shown in figure is at rest. At $t = 0$ wedge $(Y)$ is pulled toward right with constant force $(f)$ of $24$ N. Taking the block $X$ at rest at $t = 0$, the time taken by it to slide down $8.8$ m on the slope, while $Y$ is on the move, is _____ s.
(take $\tan(37°) = 3/4$ and $g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
41197.sol:
Horizontal acceleration of the wedge (assuming the block and wedge move together horizontally):
$A = \dfrac{f}{M + m} = \dfrac{24}{10 + 2} = 2\text{ m/s}^2$

Working in the non-inertial frame of the wedge, the block experiences a pseudo force $mA$ directed opposite to the wedge's acceleration. The components along the incline are:
Component of gravity down the incline: $g\sin 37^\circ$
Component of pseudo force up the incline: $A\cos 37^\circ$

Net relative acceleration of the block down the incline:
$a_{\text{rel}} = g\sin 37^\circ - A\cos 37^\circ$

Using $\sin 37^\circ = 0.6$ and $\cos 37^\circ = 0.8$:
$a_{\text{rel}} = 10(0.6) - 2(0.8) = 6 - 1.6 = 4.4\text{ m/s}^2$

Time taken to slide a distance of $8.8\text{ m}$ along the incline, starting from rest:
$s = \dfrac{1}{2} a_{\text{rel}}\, t^2$

$8.8 = \dfrac{1}{2}(4.4)\,t^2$

$8.8 = 2.2\,t^2$

$t^2 = 4 \Rightarrow t = 2\text{ s}$

Hence, the required time is $2\text{ s}$.

42692.text: When the displacement of a simple harmonic oscillator is one third of its amplitude, the ratio of total energy to the kinetic energy is $\dfrac{x}{8}$, where $x =$_________.
42692.sol:
The total energy of the harmonic oscillator is given by the formula

$E = \dfrac{1}{2}k{A}^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

where, $k$ is the force constant and $A$ is the amplitude.

The potential energy of the oscillator at the given displacement can be written as

$\begin{cases}U & = & \dfrac{1}{2}k{\left(\dfrac{A}{3}\right)}^{2} \\ & = & \dfrac{k{A}^{2}}{2 \times 9} \\ & = & \dfrac{E}{9}\end{cases}$

Hence, its kinetic energy is given by

$\begin{cases}KE & = & E - \dfrac{E}{9} \\ & = & \dfrac{8E}{9}\end{cases}$

Thus, the required ratio is

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{E}{KE} & = & \dfrac{E}{\dfrac{8E}{9}} \\ & = & \dfrac{9}{8}\end{cases}$

Hence, $x = 9$.

44817.sol: In Mollusca, each eye is located upon a stumpy peduncle called ommatophore. In Mollusca, a loose skin fold, called mantle, dorsally covers most of the body and encloses a large mantle cavity. The mantle cavity contains the rectum, genital duct, a penis in males and a small bipectinate chemoreceptor called osphradium. In Mollusca, the large oval aperture or mouth of the shell can be tightly closed by a thick, plate-like operculum attached to the foot.

44966.text: The presence of diversity at the junction of territories of two different habitats is known as
44966.sol: The presence of diversity at the junction of terretories of two different habitats is known as edge effect. In other words, the potential for the ecotone to act as habitat for species found in neither major community is called edge effect. In actual, the transition zone between two or more diverse communities is called the ecotone, the population of which becomes more adapted than both the major communities (communities of neighbouring habitats) which are too simple. In addition to this, in this region the density of most of the species is higher than that in the neighbouring.

48674.text: If the straight line $3 x+4 y=k$ touches the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=16 x$, then the value of $k$ is
48674.sol:
$\begin{aligned}&\text{ Given, } x^{2}+y^{2}=16 x \\
&\Rightarrow \quad x^{2}-16 x+y^{2}=0 \\
&\Rightarrow \quad x^{2}-2(x) 8+(8)^{2}-(8)^{2}+y^{2}=0 \\
&\Rightarrow \quad(x-8)^{2}+y^{2}=64
\end{aligned} $\therefore$ Centre $=(8,0)$ and radius $=8$
Since, the straight line 3 x+4 y=k$ touches the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=16$, therefore the length of perpendicular from the centre $(8,0)$ to the straight line $3 x+4 y-k=0$ is equal to the radius of the circle. $\begin{aligned}\text{ i.e., }& 8 &=\left|\frac{3(8)+4(0)-k}{\sqrt{9}+16}\right|\\
\Rightarrow & 8 &=\left|\frac{24-k}{\sqrt{25}}\right|\\
\Rightarrow & 8 &=\frac{|24-k|}{5}\\
\Rightarrow & & 24-k \mid &=40
\end{aligned} Taking positive sign, we get \begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow& 24-\mathrm{k}&=40 \\
\Rightarrow & &-\mathrm{k}&=40-24=16 \\
\mathrm{k}&=-16
\end{aligned} Taking negative sign, we get \begin{aligned}& \Rightarrow & 24-k &=-40 \\
\Rightarrow & &-k &=-40-24=-64 \\
& \therefore & k &=64 \\
& &=-16,64
\end{aligned}
$

55978.subject: Chemistry
55978.text: Rate constant of decomposition of hydrogen peroxide is $0.0204\ \text{minutes}^{-1}$, calculate half life of reaction.
55978.sol:
The unit of the rate constant is $\text{minutes}^{-1}$, which indicates that the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide is a first-order reaction.

For a first-order reaction, the half-life is given by:

$t_{1/2} = \dfrac{0.693}{k}$

Substituting the given value of $k = 0.0204\ \text{minutes}^{-1}$:

$t_{1/2} = \dfrac{0.693}{0.0204}$

$t_{1/2} = 33.97\ \text{minutes}$

Answer: $33.97$ minutes

To find the standard potential for the reaction $2\ \mathrm{Cu}_{(\mathrm{s})} \rightarrow 2\ \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}_{(\mathrm{aq})} + 4e^{-}$, note that this represents an oxidation process. Reversing a reaction changes the sign of $E^{}^{\circ}$, and since $E^{}^{\circ}$ is an intensive property, scaling the stoichiometry does not affect its value.

Therefore, the standard electrode potential remains $E^{}^{\circ} = -0.34\ \mathrm{V}$, corresponding to option D.

The correct answer is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

59785.subject: Chemistry
59785.text: Which of the following is effectively used to remove E. coli bacteria from water?
59785.sol:
Silver nanoparticles exhibit potent antimicrobial properties through several mechanisms that effectively eliminate E. coli. Silver ions $\mathrm{Ag^+}$ disrupt bacterial cell membrane integrity, penetrate cells to interfere with metabolic pathways, inhibit enzyme activity, and damage DNA.

Carbon black nanoparticles primarily function as adsorbents without significant intrinsic antimicrobial effects. Titanium dioxide nanoparticles $\mathrm{TiO_2}$ require UV activation for photocatalytic generation of reactive oxygen species. Silicon nanoparticles lack effective antimicrobial properties for direct bacterial removal.

Silver nanoparticles provide direct, light-independent antimicrobial action, making them the optimal choice for E. coli removal from water.

60278.text: If $2 \mathrm{f}(x)+3 \mathrm{f}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)=x^2+1, x \neq 0$ and $\mathrm{y}=5 x^2 \mathrm{f}(x)$, then y is strictly increasing in
60278.sol:
The function $y$ is strictly increasing when its derivative $\frac{dy}{dx} > 0$.

From the equation $2f(x) + 3f(\frac{1}{x}) = x^2 + 1$, replacing $x$ with $\frac{1}{x}$ yields $2f(\frac{1}{x}) + 3f(x) = \frac{1}{x^2} + 1$. Solving this system gives $f(x) = \frac{1}{5}(\frac{3}{x^2} + 1 - 2x^2)$.

Substituting into $y = 5x^2 f(x)$ yields $y = 3 + x^2 - 2x^4$. Differentiating gives $\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x - 8x^3 = 2x(1 - 4x^2) = 2x(1 - 2x)(1 + 2x)$.

The critical points are $x = -\frac{1}{2}$, $x = 0$, and $x = \frac{1}{2}$. Testing intervals shows $\frac{dy}{dx} > 0$ on $(-\infty, -\frac{1}{2})$ and $(0, \frac{1}{2})$.

Among the options, only A lies within an interval where $y$ is strictly increasing.

63171.text: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} \cos\theta & -\sin\theta \\ \sin\theta & \cos\theta \end{bmatrix}$, then the matrix $A^{-3}$ when $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$ is equal to...
63171.sol:
Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} \cos\theta & -\sin\theta \\ \sin\theta & \cos\theta \end{bmatrix}$

Using the property of rotation matrices, $A^n = \begin{bmatrix} \cos n\theta & -\sin n\theta \\ \sin n\theta & \cos n\theta \end{bmatrix}$ for any integer $n$.

For $n = -3$, we have:

$A^{-3} = \begin{bmatrix} \cos(-3\theta) & -\sin(-3\theta) \\ \sin(-3\theta) & \cos(-3\theta) \end{bmatrix}$

Since $\cos(-x) = \cos x$ and $\sin(-x) = -\sin x$, this simplifies to:

$A^{-3} = \begin{bmatrix} \cos 3\theta & \sin 3\theta \\ -\sin 3\theta & \cos 3\theta \end{bmatrix}$

Substituting $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$, we get $3\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$:

$A^{-3} = \begin{bmatrix} \cos\dfrac{\pi}{2} & \sin\dfrac{\pi}{2} \\ -\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2} & \cos\dfrac{\pi}{2} \end{bmatrix}$

$A^{-3} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$

Answer: $\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$

64362.text: If the plane $\bar{r} = (\lambda + \mu)\hat{i} + (2 + \mu)\hat{j} + (3\lambda + 2\mu)\hat{k}$, where $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are parameters, intersects coordinate axes at points $(a, 0, 0)$, $(0, b, 0)$ and $(0, 0, c)$ then $a + b + c = $...
64362.sol:
The parametric equations of the plane are given by:

$x = \lambda + \mu$

$y = 2 + \mu$

$z = 3\lambda + 2\mu$

From the second equation, we have $\mu = y - 2$.

Substituting $\mu$ into the first equation:

$x = \lambda + y - 2 \Rightarrow \lambda = x - y + 2$

Now, substituting both $\lambda$ and $\mu$ into the third equation to eliminate the parameters:

$z = 3(x - y + 2) + 2(y - 2)$

$z = 3x - 3y + 6 + 2y - 4$

$z = 3x - y + 2$

Rearranging this, we get the Cartesian equation of the plane:

$3x - y - z + 2 = 0$

To find the $x$-intercept $a$, put $y = 0$ and $z = 0$:

$3a - 0 - 0 + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow a = -\dfrac{2}{3}$

To find the $y$-intercept $b$, put $x = 0$ and $z = 0$:

$0 - b - 0 + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow b = 2$

To find the $z$-intercept $c$, put $x = 0$ and $y = 0$:

$0 - 0 - c + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow c = 2$

The sum of the intercepts is:

$a + b + c = -\dfrac{2}{3} + 2 + 2 = 4 - \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{10}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{10}{3}$

64945.text: If $\sin 3\alpha = 4\sin\alpha \cdot \sin(x+\alpha) \cdot \sin(x-\alpha)$ where $\alpha \neq n\pi, n \in \mathbb{Z}$, then all possible values of $x$ are given as
64945.sol:
Given equation is $\sin 3\alpha = 4\sin\alpha \cdot \sin(x+\alpha) \cdot \sin(x-\alpha)$

Using the identities $\sin 3\alpha = 3\sin\alpha - 4\sin^3\alpha$ and $\sin(A+B)\sin(A-B) = \sin^2 A - \sin^2 B$, we get:

$3\sin\alpha - 4\sin^3\alpha = 4\sin\alpha(\sin^2 x - \sin^2\alpha)$

$3\sin\alpha - 4\sin^3\alpha = 4\sin\alpha \sin^2 x - 4\sin^3\alpha$

$3\sin\alpha = 4\sin\alpha \sin^2 x$

Since $\alpha \neq n\pi$, $\sin\alpha \neq 0$. Dividing both sides by $\sin\alpha$, we get:

$3 = 4\sin^2 x$

$\sin^2 x = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$\sin^2 x = \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2$

$\sin^2 x = \sin^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)

The general solution is $ x = n$\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{3},$ n \in Z$.

Answer: $x = n$\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{3},$ n \in Z

66795.text: A coil of ' $n$ ' turns and resistance $R \Omega$ is connected in series with a resistance $\frac{R}{2}$. The combination is moved for time 't' second through magnetic flux $\Phi_1$ to $\Phi_2$. The induced current in the circuit is
66795.sol:
Induced current in the circuit

The total resistance is the sum of the coil resistance $R$ and the series resistance $\frac{R}{2}$, giving $R_{\text{total}} = \frac{3R}{2}$.

The magnitude of the induced EMF from Faraday's law is $\varepsilon = n \frac{(\Phi_1 - \Phi_2)}{t}$, where the flux changes from $\Phi_1$ to $\Phi_2$ in time $t$.

Applying Ohm's law, the induced current is $I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R_{\text{total}}} = \frac{n (\Phi_1 - \Phi_2)}{t} \times \frac{2}{3R} = \frac{2n (\Phi_1 - \Phi_2)}{3Rt}$.

This matches option B.

66797.text: A square of side ' $L$ ' metre lies in $x-y$ plane in a region where the magnetic field is $\vec{B}$ and $\vec{B}=B_0(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+4 \hat{k})$, where $B_0$ is constant. The magnitude of flux passing through the square (in weber) is
66797.sol:
Magnetic flux $\Phi$ through a surface is defined as the dot product of magnetic field $\mathrm{B}$ and area vector $\mathrm{A}$: $\Phi = \mathrm{B} \cdot \mathrm{A}$.

Given the square in the $x$–$y$ plane with side length $L$, its area vector is $\mathrm{A} = L^2 \hat{k}$.

For magnetic field $\mathrm{B} = B_0(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k})$, the dot product with $\mathrm{A}$ simplifies due to orthogonality of unit vectors:

$\Phi = B_0(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}) \cdot (L^2 \hat{k}) = B_0 L^2 (4\hat{k} \cdot \hat{k}) = 4 B_0 L^2$.

The magnetic flux through the square is $\Phi = 4 B_0 L^2$.

This matches option B.

68125.text: A spherical drop of liquid splits into $1000$ identical spherical drops. If $u_i$ is the surface energy of the original drop and $u_f$ is the total surface energy of the resulting drops, the (ignoring evaporation). $u_f / u_i = (10/x)$. Then value of $x$ is
68125.sol:
Let the radius of the original drop be $R$ and the radius of each smaller drop be $r$.

Equating the initial and final volumes:

$\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 1000 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$

$R^3 = 1000 r^3 \Rightarrow R = 10 r \Rightarrow r = \dfrac{R}{10}$

The initial surface energy is $u_i = T \times 4\pi R^2$.

The final total surface energy is $u_f = 1000 \times T \times 4\pi r^2$.

Substituting $r = \dfrac{R}{10}$:

$u_f = 1000 \times T \times 4\pi \left(\dfrac{R}{10}\right)^2 = 10 \times T \times 4\pi R^2 = 10 u_i$

The ratio is $\dfrac{u_f}{u_i} = 10$.

Given $\dfrac{u_f}{u_i} = \dfrac{10}{x}$, we get $x = 1$.

Answer: $1$

69443.text: When the conductivity of a semiconductor is only due to breaking of covalent bonds, the semiconductor is called
69443.sol:
In a pure semiconductor, the conductivity is solely due to the thermal excitation of electrons from the valence band to the conduction band, which occurs by the breaking of covalent bonds. Such a semiconductor, without any added impurities, is called an intrinsic semiconductor.

Extrinsic semiconductors (p-type and n-type) have their conductivity significantly enhanced by the addition of specific impurities (doping).

Answer: intrinsic.

69725.text: A black disc has a radius 'R' and wavelength corresponding to the maximum intensity is '$\lambda$'. The emissive power (E) for the different radii and maximum wavelengths is directly proportional to
69725.sol:
The total emissive power of a black body is given by the Stefan-Boltzmann law:

$E = A \sigma T^4$

For a disc of radius $R$, the surface area $A \propto R^2$. Therefore, the emissive power is proportional to:

$E \propto R^2 T^4$

According to Wien's displacement law, the wavelength corresponding to maximum intensity $\lambda$ is related to the absolute temperature $T$ as:

$\lambda T = b$

$T \propto \lambda^{-1}$

Substituting this into the proportionality for $E$, we get:

$E \propto R^2 (\lambda^{-1})^4$

$E \propto R^2 \lambda^{-4}$

Answer: $R^2, \lambda^{-4}$

69935.text: An ideal gas undergoes cyclic process ABCDA as shown in given p-V diagram. What is the magnitude of amount of work done by the gas?
69935.sol:
The magnitude of work done by the gas in a cyclic process is equal to the area enclosed by the cycle on the $P-V$ diagram.

The given cycle $ABCDA$ forms a rectangle.

The width of the rectangle along the volume axis is $\Delta V = 5V_0 - 3V_0 = 2V_0$.

The height of the rectangle along the pressure axis is $\Delta P = 4P_0 - 2P_0 = 2P_0$.

Magnitude of work done $|W| = \text{Area of rectangle } ABCD$

$|W| = \Delta P \times \Delta V$

$|W| = (2P_0) \times (2V_0) = 4P_0V_0$.

Answer: $4 P_0 V_0$

70494.subject: Physics
70494.text: A pipe open at both ends produces a fundamental frequency $n_1$. When the pipe is kept with $\frac{3}{4}^{\text{th }}$ of its length in water, it produces a note of fundamental frequency $n_2$. The ratio of $\frac{n_1}{n_2}$ is
70494.sol:
A pipe of length $L$ has fundamental frequency $n_1 = \frac{v}{2L}$ when open at both ends.

When $\frac{3}{4}$ of the pipe is submerged in water, the remaining $\frac{1}{4}L$ length of air column behaves as a closed pipe, with fundamental frequency $n_2 = \frac{v}{4 \cdot \frac{1}{4}L} = \frac{v}{L}$.

The ratio of frequencies is therefore $\frac{n_1}{n_2} = \frac{\frac{v}{2L}}{\frac{v}{L}} = \frac{1}{2}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

71716.subject: Chemistry
71716.text: Which of the following are not used for the treatment of humans?
71716.sol:
Antiseptics are chemical substances which prevent the growth of microorganisms or kill them and are safe to be applied to living tissues such as wounds, cuts, ulcers, and diseased skin surfaces.

Disinfectants are chemical substances which kill microorganisms but are not safe to be applied to living tissues. They are generally applied to inanimate objects such as floors, drainage systems, and instruments.

Antimalarials and antibiotics are drugs used for the treatment of diseases in humans.

Therefore, disinfectants are not used for the treatment of humans.

Answer: Disinfectants

71768.subject: Chemistry
71768.text: How many Faraday electricity is required to reduce 0.25 g of Nb(V) to the metal? ( Atomic mass of Nb = 93)
71768.sol:
The reduction reaction of Nb(V) to Nb metal is given by:

$Nb^{5+} + 5e^{-} \rightarrow Nb$

This indicates that $5$ moles of electrons (or $5$ Faradays of electricity) are required to reduce $1$ mole of Nb(V) to Nb metal.

Number of moles of Nb in $0.25$ g is:

$n = \dfrac{0.25}{93}$

The number of Faradays required is:

$Q = 5 \times n = 5 \times \dfrac{0.25}{93} = \dfrac{1.25}{93}$

$Q \approx 0.01344 \text{ F} = 1.34 \times 10^{-2} \text{ F}$

Answer: $1.3\times10^{-2}$

72033.subject: Chemistry
72033.text: Calculate $\Delta H$ for a reaction, $2X_{(g)} + Y_{(g)} \rightarrow 2Z_{(g)}$ at $298$ K if $\Delta U = -10.5$ kJ and $R = 8.314\ \text{J K}^{-1}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$.
72033.sol:
For the given reaction $2X_{(g)} + Y_{(g)} \rightarrow 2Z_{(g)}$, the change in the number of moles of gaseous species is:

$\Delta n_g = \text{moles of gaseous products} - \text{moles of gaseous reactants}$

$\Delta n_g = 2 - (2 + 1) = -1$

The relationship between enthalpy change (\Delta H$) and internal energy change (\Delta U$) is given by:

$\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta H = -10.5 \text{ kJ} + (-1) \times (8.314 \times 10^{-3} \text{ kJ K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}) \times 298 \text{ K}$

$\Delta H = -10.5 \text{ kJ} - 2.477 \text{ kJ}$

$\Delta H = -12.977 \text{ kJ} \approx -12.98 \text{ kJ}$

Answer: $-12.98$ kJ
72033.meta: Calculate Δ H for a reaction, 2X_ (g) + Y_ (g) arrow 2Z_ (g) at 298 K if Δ U = -10.5 kJ and R = 8.314\ J K^ -1 \ mol^ -1 .

Directions: Identify which part of the given sentence contains a grammatical error.

Of all the players it was Ramesh who plan his tactics with utmost care.
72576.sol:
The sentence is in the past tense, as indicated by the phrase "it was Ramesh". Therefore, the verb following the relative pronoun "who" must also be in the past tense to maintain consistency. The verb "plan" should be replaced with "planned".

The correct sentence is: "Of all the players it was Ramesh who planned his tactics with utmost care."

Hence, the error lies in the part "who plan his tactics".

72580.text:
Fill in the blanks $(X, Y)$ in the following sentences with the appropriate word/phrase given in the brackets:
I. I spent $X$ (less/the least) money on clothes in the whole family.

72580.sol:
In sentence I, the comparison is made among all the members of the family, which requires the superlative degree. Since 'money' is an uncountable noun, 'the least' is the correct phrase.

In sentence II, the comparison is again in the superlative degree as indicated by 'the hardest'. Since 'mistakes' is a plural countable noun, 'the fewest' is the correct phrase.

Thus, X is 'the least' and Y is 'the fewest'.

Answer: I - the least, II - the fewest

73821.subject: General Ability
73821.text: Which one of the following oxides is a neutral oxide?
73821.sol:
Oxides can be classified as acidic, basic, amphoteric, or neutral based on their acid-base characteristics.

$CO$ (Carbon monoxide) is a neutral oxide because it neither reacts with acids nor with bases to form salts.

$CO_2$ is an acidic oxide as it reacts with water to form carbonic acid.

$Na_2O$ and $MgO$ are metallic oxides, which are basic in nature.

Other common examples of neutral oxides include $N_2O$ and $NO$.

Answer: $CO$

76811.subject: Mathematics
76811.text: If $\int_0^{\pi / 2}\left(\sin ^4 x+\cos ^4 x\right) d x=k$, then what is the value of $\int_0^{20 \pi}\left(\sin ^4+\cos ^4 x\right) d x ?$
76811.sol:
Concept:
If $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ is a periodic function with period T , then $\int_0^{n T} f(x) d x=n \int_0^T f(x) d x$ If $f(x)$ is periodic with period $T$, then $f(a x)$ is periodic with period $\frac{T}{|a|}$
Calculation:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{ Let } f(x)=\left(\sin ^4 x+\cos ^4 x\right) \\
& \Rightarrow f(x)=\left(\sin ^2 x\right)^2+\left(\cos ^2 x\right)^2+2 \sin ^2 x \cos ^2 x-2 \sin ^2 x \cos ^2 x \\
& \Rightarrow f(x)=\left(\sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x\right)^2-2 \sin ^2 x \cos ^2 x \\
& \Rightarrow f(x)=1-\frac{\sin ^2 2 x}{2} \\
& \Rightarrow f(x)=1-\frac{1-\cos 4 x}{4} \\
& \Rightarrow f(x)=\frac{3}{4}+\frac{\cos 4 x}{4}
\end{aligned}$
Since $\cos x$ is a function of period $2 \pi\Rightarrow \cos 4 x$ is periodic with period $\frac{2 \pi}{4}=\frac{\pi}{2}\Rightarrow f(x)=  \left(\sin ^4 x+\cos ^4 x\right)$ is periodic with period $\frac{\pi}{2}$
Given, $\int_0^{\pi / 2}\left(\sin ^4 x+\cos ^4 x\right) d x=k\qquad$
So, $\int_0^{20 \pi}\left(\sin ^4 x+\cos ^4 x\right) d x=\int_0^{40  \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)}\left(\sin ^4 x+\cos ^4 x\right) d x$
As $f(x)=\left(\sin ^4 x+\cos ^4 x\right)$ is periodic with period $\frac{\pi}{2}$
By the property of definite integral,
$\begin{aligned}
& \int_0^{40\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)}\left(\sin ^4 x+\cos ^4 x\right) d x=40 \int_0^{\pi / 2}\left(\sin ^4 x+\cos ^4 x\right) d x \\
& \Rightarrow \int_0^{20 \pi}\left(\sin ^4 x+\cos ^4 x\right) d x=40 k\{\text{ Using }(i)\}
\end{aligned}$

77564.subject: Mathematics
77564.sol:
Let $A = \cot^{-1} 9 \Rightarrow \cot A = 9 \Rightarrow \tan A = \dfrac{1}{9}$

Let $B = \text{cosec}^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{41}}{4}\right) \Rightarrow \text{cosec} B = \dfrac{\sqrt{41}}{4} \Rightarrow \sin B = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{41}}$

From this, $\tan B = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{(\sqrt{41})^2 - 4^2}} = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{41 - 16}} = \dfrac{4}{5}$

Using the formula $\tan(A + B) = \dfrac{\tan A + \tan B}{1 - \tan A \tan B}$:

$\tan(A + B) = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{9} + \dfrac{4}{5}}{1 - \left(\dfrac{1}{9}\right)\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right)}$

$\tan(A + B) = \dfrac{\dfrac{5 + 36}{45}}{\dfrac{45 - 4}{45}}$

$\tan(A + B) = \dfrac{41}{41} = 1$

Since $A, B \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right), we have $A + B = $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$$

Answer: \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

79952.subject: Botany
79952.text:
What type of ecological pyramid would be obtained with following data?
Secondary consumer : 120 g
Primary consumer : 60 g
Primary producer : 10 g
79952.sol:
The inverted pyramid of biomass

Biomass is the amount of living material in an organism. The pyramids of biomass represent the relationship between different trophic levels in terms of biomass. In grassland and forest ecosystems, there is generally a gradual decrease in the biomass of organisms at successive trophic levels from the producers to the consumers. Their pyramid of biomass is upright. In an aquatic ecosystem, the producers are small organisms with the least biomass and the biomass gradually increase towards the apex of the pyramid. Thus, the pyramid of the biomass of aquatic ecosystems is inverted in shape.

80726.subject: Chemistry
80726.text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding amino acids ?
A. They are substituted methanes.
B. Serine is an aromatic amino acid.
C. Valine is a neutral amino acid.
D. Lysine is an acidic amino acid.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
80726.sol:
Amino acids are organic compounds containing an amino group and an acidic group as substituents on the same carbon, i.e., the $\alpha$-carbon. Therefore, they are considered substituted methanes. Statement A is correct.

Serine contains a hydroxymethyl group ($\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$) as its side chain and is an aliphatic amino acid, not an aromatic one. Aromatic amino acids include phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan. Statement B is incorrect.

Valine contains one amino group and one carboxyl group, making it a neutral amino acid. Statement C is correct.

Lysine contains two amino groups and one carboxyl group, making it a basic amino acid, not an acidic one. Acidic amino acids include aspartic acid and glutamic acid. Statement D is incorrect.

Thus, only statements A and C are correct.

Answer: A and C only

82996.subject: Physics
82996.text: A vibration magnetometer placed in magnetic meridian has a small bar magnet. The magnet executes oscillations with a time period of $2 \mathrm{~s}$ in earth's horizontal magnetic field of $24 \mu \mathrm{T}$. When a horizontal field of $18 \mu \mathrm{T}$ is produced opposite to the earth's field by placing a current carrying wire, the new time period of magnet will be
82996.sol:
The time period T of oscillation of a magnet is given by
\(T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{I}{M B}}\)
where,
I = Moment of inertia of the magnet about the axis of rotation
\(M=\) Magnetic moment of the magnet
\(B=\) Uniform magnetic field As I, B remains the same
\(\therefore \quad T \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{B}}\) or \(\frac{T_2}{T_1}=\sqrt{\frac{B_1}{B_2}}\)
According to given problem,
$\begin{aligned}
B_1 & =24 \mu \mathrm{T} \\
B_2 & =24 \mu \mathrm{T}-18 \mu \mathrm{T}=6 \mu \mathrm{T} \\
T_1 & =2 \mathrm{~s} \\
\therefore \quad T_2 & =(2 \mathrm{~s}) \sqrt{\frac{(24 \mu \mathrm{T})}{(6 \mu \mathrm{T})}}=4 \mathrm{~s}
\end{aligned}\)$

84046.subject: Zoology
84046.text: The number of action potentials generated by sino-arterial node (SAN) in a healthy human is __________ per minute.
84046.sol:
The sino-atrial node (SAN) is a specialised patch of cardiac musculature present in the right upper corner of the right atrium.

It has the ability to generate action potentials without any external stimuli, making it autoexcitable.

The SAN can generate the maximum number of action potentials, which is $70-75$ per minute in a healthy human.

This rate of action potential generation is responsible for initiating and maintaining the rhythmic contractile activity of the heart, which is why the SAN is called the pacemaker. Consequently, the normal human heart beats $70-75$ times per minute (average $72$ beats per minute).

85139.subject: Zoology
85139.text: Praying mantis is a good example of:
85139.sol: Praying mantis (Mantis religiosa) is a large social insect. Social insects are the ants, bees, wasps, and termites that have organized societies and live in colonies. They have one or a few females responsible for all the egg laying, while other members of the colony (usually sterile females) gather food and do other tasks. Camouflage or cryptic colouration is a defence mechanism that helps insects merge with their surroundings. They do it to conceal their presence or identity, either to hoodwink their predators or to deceive their prey. Müllerian mimicry is a form of biological resemblance in which two or more unrelated noxious, or dangerous, organisms and exhibit closely similar warning systems, such as the same pattern of bright colours. Warning colouration (or aposematism) is how animals let other animals know that they are poisonous or dangerous.

87672.text:
At $407K$ the rate constant of a chemical reaction is $9.5 \times 1{0}^{- 5}{s}^{- 1}$ and at $420K$ , the rate constant is $1.9 \times 1{0}^{- 4}{s}^{- 1}$ . The frequency factor of the reaction is $x \times 1{0}^{5}{s}^{- 1}$ .The value of 'x' is.
Report your answer by rounding it up to nearest whole number.
87672.sol:
The Arrhenius equation is,
${\text\log}_{{10}^{}} \dfrac{{\text{k}}_{\text{2}}}{{\text{k}}_{\text{1}}} = \dfrac{{\text{E}}_{\text{a}}}{\text{2}\text{.303 \times R}} \left[\dfrac{{\text{T}}_{\text{2}} - {\text{T}}_{\text{1}}}{{\text{T}}_{\text{1}} {\text{T}}_{\text{2}}}\right]$
Given ${\text{k}}_{\text{1}} = 9.5 \times {10}^{- 5} {\text{s}}^{- \text{1}} \text{;}{\text{k}}_{\text{2}} = 1.9 \times {10}^{- 3} {\text{s}}^{- 1}$
$\text{R} = 8.314{\text{Jmol}}^{- 1} {\text{K}}^{- 1}$;
${T}_{1} = 407K$ and ${T}_{2} = 420K$
Substituting the values in Arrhenius equation.
$\text{lo}{\text{g}}_{10}\dfrac{1.9 \times 1{0}^{- 4}}{9.5 \times 1{0}^{- 5}} = \dfrac{{E}_{a}}{2.303 \times 8.314}\left[\dfrac{420 - 407}{420 \times 407}\right]$
${E}_{a} = 75782.3J\text{mo}{\text{l}}^{- 1}$
Applying now $log ⁡ {k}_{1} = log ⁡ A - \dfrac{{E}_{a}}{2.303R{T}_{1}}$
$log ⁡ 9.5 \times {10}^{- 5} = log ⁡ A - \dfrac{75782.3}{2.303 \times 8.314 \times 407}$
$\text\log\dfrac{\text{A}}{9.5 \times {10}^{- 5}} = \dfrac{75782.3}{2.303 \times 8.314 \times 407} = 9.7246$
So, $A = 5.0 \times 1{0}^{5}{s}^{- 1}$

Let ${R}_{i} ( i = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 )$ denotes $1, 2, 3, 4$ or $5$ red balls in the bag. Let $R$ represent the ball drawn is red, then
$P ( {R}_{1} ) = P ( {R}_{2} ) = P ( {R}_{3} ) = P ( {R}_{4} ) = P ( {R}_{5} ) = \dfrac{1}{5}$
$andP\left(\dfrac{R}{{R}_{1}}\right) = \dfrac{1}{5}, P\left(\dfrac{R}{{R}_{2}}\right) = \dfrac{2}{5}, P\left(\dfrac{R}{{R}_{3}}\right) = \dfrac{3}{5}, P\left(\dfrac{R}{{R}_{4}}\right) = \dfrac{4}{5}$
$P\left(\dfrac{R}{{R}_{5}}\right) = 1$
$∴ P\left(\dfrac{{R}_{5}}{R}\right) = \dfrac{P ( {R}_{5} ) ⋅ P\left(\dfrac{R}{{R}_{5}}\right)}{\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{5}P ( {R}_{i} ) ⋅ P\left(\dfrac{R}{{R}_{i}}\right)}$
$= \dfrac{1}{1 + \dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{2}{5} + \dfrac{3}{5} + \dfrac{4}{5}} = \dfrac{5}{15} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

93323.text: Gravitational acceleration on the surface of a planet is $\dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{11}g$ , where g is the gravitational acceleration on the surface of the earth. The average mass density of the planet is $\dfrac{2}{3}$ times that of the earth. If the escape speed on the surface of the earth is taken to be 11 km/s, the escape speed on the surface of the planet in km/s will be
93323.sol:
$g = \dfrac{GM}{R^{2}} = \dfrac{G}{R^{2}}\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}ρ = \dfrac{4}{3}\piGRρ$ i.e. $g ∝ Rρ$

$\dfrac{{g}_{P}}{{g}_{E}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{6}{g}_{E}}{11{g}_{E}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{11}$ and $\dfrac{{ρ}_{E}}{{ρ}_{P}} = \dfrac{3}{2}$ and $\dfrac{{g}_{P}}{{g}_{E}} = \dfrac{{R}_{P}{ρ}_{P}}{{R}_{E}{ρ}_{E}}$

$∴ \dfrac{{R}_{P}}{{R}_{E}} = \dfrac{{g}_{P}{ρ}_{E}}{{g}_{E}{ρ}_{P}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{11} \times \dfrac{3}{2}$

$∴$ Escape velocity $v = \sqrt{2gR}$

$∴ \dfrac{{v}_{P}}{{v}_{E}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{g}_{P}}{{g}_{E}} \times \dfrac{{R}_{P}}{{R}_{E}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{11} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{11} \times \dfrac{3}{2}}= \dfrac{3}{11}$

$∴ {v}_{P} = \dfrac{3}{11} \times {v}_{E} = \dfrac{3}{11} \times 11 = 3kms^{- 1}$

93591.text: A cylindrical conductor of radius $R$ carrying current $i$ along the axis such that the magnetic field inside the conductor varies as $B = {B}_{0}{r}^{2}\left(0 < r \le R\right)$, then which of the following is incorrect?
options: Current density at distance ‘r’ from central axis of the conductor is $J(r) = \dfrac{2{B}_{0}r}{{\mu}_{0}}$
Current density at distance ‘r’ from central axis of the conductor is $J(r) = \dfrac{3{B}_{0}r}{{\mu}_{0}}$

93591.sol:
Hint: Use Ampere’s law
Sol: As $B\left(r\right) = {B}_{0}{r}^{2}$



$∴$ Total current (upto R)
${B}_{0}{R}^{2}2\piR = {\mu}_{0}{I}_{0} ⇒ {I}_{0} = \dfrac{2\pi{R}^{3}{B}_{0}}{{\mu}_{0}}$
And let upto 'r' it confines half of the current.

Then ${B}_{0}{r'}^{2} \cdot 2\pir' = {\mu}_{0}\dfrac{{I}_{0}}{2}$
$⇒ {B}_{0} \cdot 2\pi{r'}^{3} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{2} \cdot \dfrac{2\pi{R}^{3}{B}_{0}}{{\mu}_{0}}$
$⇒ r' = \dfrac{R}{{\left(2\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}}$

Now let $\overset{\to}{J}(r)$ is the current density at ‘r’
Then ${B}_{0}{r}^{2} \cdot 2\pir = {\mu}_{0}{∫}_{0}^{r}J(r)2\pirdr$
$∵ \left({∫}_{}^{}Bdl = {\mu}_{0}I\right)$
$⇒ 2\pi{B}_{0}{r}^{3} = {\mu}_{0} \cdot 2\pi{∫}_{0}^{r}J(r)rdr$

$∴$ Differentiating both side w.r.t(r)
$2\pi{B}_{0} \cdot 3{r}^{2} \cdot dr = {\mu}_{0}2\pi \cdot J(r)rdr$
$⇒ J(r) = \dfrac{3{B}_{0}r}{{\mu}_{0}}$

For $r > R$;

$B \times 2\pir = {\mu}_{0}{I}_{0}$

$⇒ B \times 2\pir = {\mu}_{0} \times \dfrac{2\pi{R}^{3}{B}_{0}}{{\mu}_{0}}$

$⇒ B = \dfrac{{B}_{0}{R}^{3}}{r}$

94703.text: A Carnot engine whose low-temperature reservoir is at $350K$ has an efficiency of $50%$ . It is desired to increase the efficiency to $60%$. If the temperature of the low-temperature reservoir is kept constant, then by how many kelvins the temperature of the high-temperature reservoir must be increased to get the desired efficiency?
94703.sol:
The efficiency of the Carnot engine,

$η = 1 - \dfrac{{T}_{cold}}{{T}_{hot}} \times 100$

When $η = 50%$

then $\dfrac{50}{100} = 1 - \dfrac{{T}_{cold}}{{T}_{hot}} ⇒ 0.5 = 1 - \dfrac{350}{{T}_{hot}}$

or ${T}_{hot} = 700K$

When $η = 60%$

then $\dfrac{60}{100} = 1 - \dfrac{{T}_{cold}}{{T}_{hot}} ⇒ 0.6 = 1 - \dfrac{350}{{T}_{hot}}$

or ${T}_{hot} = 875K$

Hence, the temperature of the high reservoir is increased by

$T{′}_{hot} - {T}_{hot} = 875K - 700K = 175K$

Snails are generally intermediate hosts. These belong to Phylum Platyhelminthes. The word Platy means flat. Hence these are commonly known as flat worms and thus their body is dorsoventrally flat. These organisms also show bilateral symmetry and are acoelomates which means they lack body cavity due to flat body This Phylum is evolved than earlier phyla due to presence of third germ layer i.e. Mesoderm. 96257.subject: Botany
96257.text: Select the correct even from below that is most likely to occur during the three subphases of the interphase of the mitotic cell cycle.
options: During G_{1} phase, the cell is metabolically active and replicates its DNA.&
During S phase, duplication of centrioles takes place.
The number of chromosomes becomes double in the synthesis phase.
Replication of DNA starts during the G_{2} phase and proteins are synthesized in order to prepare the cell for mitosis.
96257.sol: Interphase can be subdivided into 3 further phase: G_{1}, S and G_{2}. G_{1} phase corresponds to the interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication. During G_{1} phase the cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA. S or synthesis phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place. During this time the amount of DNA per cell doubles. If the initial amount of DNA is denoted as 2C then it increases to 4C. However, there is no increase in the chromosome number; if the cell had diploid or 2n number of chromosomes at G_{1}, even after S phase the number of chromosomes remains the same, i.e., 2n. In animal cells, during the S phase, DNA replication begins in the nucleus, and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm. During the G_{2} phase, proteins are synthesised in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues

97113.text:
Go through the following matches regarding the flower and ovary position.

(i) Mustard - Epigynous
(ii) Plum - Perigynous
(iii) Hibiscus - Epigynous
(iv) Peach - Perigynous

Which of these is/are CORRECT?
97113.sol:
A flower may be hypogynous, perigynous or epigynous on the basis of position of calyx, corolla and androecium in respect to the ovary. Ovary occupies the highest position in hypogynous flower while other parts are situated below the ovary. In perigynous flowers gynoecium is situated at the centre while other parts are situated on the rim of the thalamus. In epigynous flowers ovary is completely enclosed by thalamus, other floral parts arise above the ovary. Perigynous flowers are found in Plum and Peach.

Hypogynous flowers are found in Hibiscus and Mustard.

97504.subject: Botany
97504.text: Recognise the figure and find out the CORRECT matching:
options: a-Haplontic life cycle, b-diplontic life cycle, c-haplodiplontic life cycle
a-Haplodiplontic life cycle, b-diplontic life cycle, c-haplontic life cycle
a-Diplontic life cycle, b-haplodiplontic life cycle, c-haplontic life cycle
a-Haplontic life cycle, b-haplodiplontic life cycle, c-diplontic life cycle
97504.sol:
The alternation of the two phases of life cycle between sexual phase and asexual phase is called alternation of generation. Such life cycle pattern is commonly observed in plants and algae. It is also called metagenesis and in it haploid gametophytic (generally sexual) generation alternates with diploid sporophytic (generally asexual) generation.

There are three variations in the life cycle. In diplontic life cycle, the sporophyte is diploid, dominant, autotrophic and independent. The gametophytic generation is haploid, recessive and dependent on sporophyte. The duration of sporophyte is longer than gametophyte generation. Observed in Angiosperms.

In haplontic life cycle, the gametophyte stage is dominant, green, haploid and independent while the sporophyte stage is diploid, recessive and partially dependent on gametophyte. Also, the gametophytic stage duration is longer than the sporophytic stage. Observed in algae.

In haplodiplontic life cycle, both the stages have nearly equal duration and none of them are dominant. Gametophyte is represented as independent, autotrophic and haploid. Whereas the sporophyte is independent, autotrophic and diploid. Pteridophytes show such life cycle.

97887.subject: Botany
options: The first word in a biological name represents the genus while the second component denotes the specific epithet.
Biological names are generally in the Latin language.

Both the words in a biological name, when handwritten, are
separately underlined, or printed in Latin.
The first word denoting the genus starts with a capital letter& while the specific epithet starts with a small letter.&
97887.sol:
Universal rules of nomenclature are as follows:

1. Biological names are generally in Latin and written in italics. They are Latinised or derived from Latin irrespective of their origin.
2. The first word in a biological name represents the genus while the second component denotes the specific epithet.
3. Both the words in a biological name, when handwritten, are separately underlined, or printed in italics to indicate their Latin origin.
4. The first word denoting the genus starts with a capital letter while the specific epithet starts with a small letter. It can be illustrated with the example of Mangifera indica.

97900.subject: Botany
97900.text: The earliest attempt to the scientific basis for classification is made by
97900.sol: Aristotle was a Greek philosopher who classified the living organisms on a scientific basis for the first time. He classified the plants as herbs, shrubs and trees and animals were categorized into two groups, animals with red blood and animals without red blood. The need for a higher and a better classification was always felt. Linnaeus was responsible for the two kingdom classification (Plantae and Animalia) and R.H.Whittaker introduced the five-kingdom classification whose main basis was the mode of nutrition. Theophrastus was a successor to Aristotle and was known for classifying plants and how they reproduced.

100503.subject: Physics
100503.text: A projectile is fired from the surface of the earth with an initial speed of $40 \mathrm{~m/s}$. If its speed at the highest point of its trajectory is exactly half of its initial projection speed, what is the maximum height attained by the projectile? (Take $g = 10 \mathrm{~m/s^2}$ and neglect air resistance)
100503.sol:
Let the initial speed be $u$ and the angle of projection with the horizontal be $\theta$.

At the highest point of the trajectory, the vertical component of velocity becomes zero, and the projectile only has a horizontal component of velocity, which remains constant throughout the motion. Thus, the speed at the highest point is $v = u \cos\theta$.

Given that the speed at the highest point is half of the initial speed:
$u \cos\theta = \dfrac{u}{2}$
$\cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{2} \implies \theta = 60^{\circ}$

The maximum height $H$ is given by the formula:
$H = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g}$

Substituting $u = 40 \mathrm{~m/s}$, $\theta = 60^{\circ}$, and $g = 10 \mathrm{~m/s^2}$:
$H = \dfrac{(40)^2 \times (\sin 60^{\circ})^2}{2 \times 10}$
$H = \dfrac{1600 \times \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2}{20}$
$H = \dfrac{1600 \times \dfrac{3}{4}}{20} = \dfrac{1200}{20} = 60 \mathrm{~m}$

Answer: $60 \mathrm{~m}$

102453.subject: Physics
102453.text: A particle of mass $m$ in the $xy$-plane experiences a two-dimensional restoring force given by $\vec{F} = -k(x \hat{i} + y \hat{j})$, where $k$ is a positive constant. The particle is displaced to a point $P(x_0, y_0)$, where $x_0$ and $y_0$ are non-zero and unequal, and is released from rest at $t=0$. The shape of the trajectory of the particle will be a/an:
102453.sol:
The force acting on the particle is $\vec{F} = -kx \hat{i} - ky \hat{j}$.

This can be resolved into two independent components: $F_x = -kx$ and $F_y = -ky$.

These represent independent simple harmonic motions along the $x$ and $y$ axes with the same angular frequency $\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$.

The general equations for the displacements are $x(t) = A_x \cos(\omega t + \phi_x)$ and $y(t) = A_y \cos(\omega t + \phi_y)$.

Since the particle is released from rest at $t=0$ from the point $(x_0, y_0)$, its initial velocity components are zero. This means it starts from the extreme positions for both $x$ and $y$ motions simultaneously. Therefore, the phase constants are zero (or equal), and the amplitudes are $x_0$ and $y_0$.

The equations of motion become $x(t) = x_0 \cos(\omega t)$ and $y(t) = y_0 \cos(\omega t)$.

Dividing the $y$-equation by the $x$-equation gives $\dfrac{y}{x} = \dfrac{y_0}{x_0}$, which simplifies to $y = \left(\dfrac{y_0}{x_0}\right) x$.

This is a linear equation representing a straight line passing through the origin.

Answer: straight line

103682.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The magnetic field at a distance $x = R$ on the axis of a circular current-carrying coil of radius $R$ is $\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}$ times the magnetic field at its centre.
Reason (R): The magnetic field on the axis of a circular coil varies inversely as the cube of the distance from the centre ($B \propto \dfrac{1}{x^3}$) for distances much greater than the radius ($x \gg R$).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct
103682.sol:
Assertion: The magnetic field on the axis of a circular coil is $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}$.
At $x = R$, $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(2R^2)^{3/2}} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R} \times \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{B_c}{2\sqrt{2}}$.
Thus, the Assertion is correct.

Reason: For $x \gg R$, the term $R^2$ can be neglected in the denominator.
$B \approx \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(x^2)^{3/2}} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2x^3}$.
So, $B \propto \dfrac{1}{x^3}$.
Thus, the Reason is correct.

However, the Reason describes a far-field approximation ($x \gg R$) which cannot be used to derive the exact magnetic field at a near-field point ($x = R$). The exact formula must be used for $x = R$. Therefore, the Reason is not the correct explanation for the Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

105261.subject: Physics
105261.text: A heavily doped $p$-$n$ junction diode undergoes Zener breakdown at a reverse bias voltage of $5\text{ V}$. Which of the following correctly explains the primary mechanism responsible for this breakdown?
options: Minority carriers gain high kinetic energy from the electric field and break covalent bonds through collisions.
A very high electric field across the thin depletion region directly pulls electrons from covalent bonds.
The wide depletion region generates excessive heat under reverse bias, causing thermal breakdown of the junction.
Majority carriers easily cross the junction due to a significant decrease in the barrier potential under reverse bias.
105261.sol:
Zener breakdown occurs in heavily doped $p$-$n$ junction diodes. Heavy doping results in a very thin depletion region.

Even at a relatively low reverse bias voltage (like $5\text{ V}$), the electric field across the extremely thin depletion region becomes very high ($E = V/d$).

This intense electric field is sufficient to directly pull electrons out of covalent bonds, creating a large number of electron-hole pairs. This process is known as internal field emission.

Option 1 describes avalanche breakdown, which occurs in lightly doped diodes with wider depletion regions. Option 3 incorrectly assumes a wide depletion region and thermal breakdown. Option 4 describes forward bias operation, not reverse breakdown.

Answer: A very high electric field across the thin depletion region directly pulls electrons from covalent bonds.

107767.subject: Chemistry
107767.text: The correct decreasing order of dipole moments for the molecules $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$, $\mathrm{NH}_3$, $\mathrm{NF}_3$ and $\mathrm{BF}_3$ is
107767.sol:
The dipole moment of a molecule depends on its geometry and the vector addition of bond dipoles and lone pair dipoles.

$\mathrm{BF}_3$ has a symmetrical trigonal planar geometry, so the bond dipoles cancel out exactly, resulting in a net dipole moment of zero.

In $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$, the molecule is bent with two lone pairs. The highly polar $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ bonds and the two lone pairs strongly reinforce each other, giving it the highest dipole moment among the given molecules ($1.85\text{ D}$).

In $\mathrm{NH}_3$, the lone pair orbital dipole is in the same direction as the resultant of the three $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{H}$ bond dipoles, leading to a high net dipole moment ($1.47\text{ D}$).

In $\mathrm{NF}_3$, the lone pair orbital dipole is in the opposite direction to the resultant of the three $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{F}$ bond dipoles. This partial cancellation results in a much lower net dipole moment ($0.23\text{ D}$) compared to $\mathrm{NH}_3$.

Therefore, the correct decreasing order is $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} > \mathrm{NH}_3 > \mathrm{NF}_3 > \mathrm{BF}_3$.
